h1: Hansar Bangkok — a quiet boutique all-suite retreat on Soi Ratchadamri 2, with an infinity pool overlooking the Royal Sports Club and BTS Ratchadamri three minutes away
intro: Hansar Bangkok is a 5-star boutique all-suite hotel tucked into Soi Mahadlekluang 2 (Soi Ratchadamri 2) off Rajadamri Road — three minutes on foot from BTS Ratchadamri, yet far quieter than its main-road neighbours. Every one of the 94 rooms is a suite, ranging from 59 to 125 sqm, decorated with Jim Thompson silk fabrics, marble bathrooms and floor-to-ceiling windows. The property faces the Royal Bangkok Sports Club, so rooms on that side open directly onto a sweep of green fairways — a surprisingly calm visual in the centre of Bangkok that guest reviews single out again and again. Breakfast for two is included in every suite at no extra charge. The 8th-floor infinity-edge pool and Jacuzzi overlook the same golf course, and the hotel runs two dedicated wellness facilities: Hansar Thai Wellness for traditional massage and Luxsa Clinic, a certified medical wellness centre. Dining options include Arizuki (an acclaimed Japanese restaurant with a Japan-trained chef), Elefin Café, Italian Osteria and Rouge Bar. The hotel scores 8.7/10 from 810 verified Booking.com reviews and 9.0 from 134 Trip.com reviewers. Prices start from approx. THB 3,800/night (breakfast included) outside the high season — a genuinely compelling rate for a property of this suite-size and calibre.

body.html: Soi Mahadlekluang 2 is one of those Bangkok addresses that means little until you check the map — it turns out to be a calm residential lane running off Rajadamri Road between BTS Ratchadamri and the BTS Chidlom corridor, with the vast green expanse of the Royal Bangkok Sports Club immediately alongside it. Hansar opened on this lane in 2010 with a deliberate positioning: not the grandest lobby or the largest conference suite, but a fully all-suite property where the smallest room is bigger than most superior rooms at Bangkok's mid-range hotels, and every suite comes with its own living area, proper workspace and floor-to-ceiling windows. Guest reviews consistently describe first impressions as pleasantly surprising — "the room is much larger than I expected" features in dozens of recent write-ups across Booking.com and Trip.com.

The 94 suites across 19 floors divide into six categories. The Luxury Suite at 59 sqm is the entry level, decorated in warm Jim Thompson silks with a marble bathroom combining both a rain shower and a deep soaking bath. The Urban Suite at 71 sqm adds a full-height living green wall of real plants, dual televisions and a larger minibar — several reviews pick this as the best value-to-space ratio in the house. The Horizon Suite (59 sqm) earns its name from a direct view over the Royal Sports Club's fairways; the Edge Suite (77 sqm) adds a private balcony; the Vertigo Suite (82 sqm) rises higher for a wider city panorama; and the Duplex Suite at 125 sqm on two levels has a fully separated bedroom upstairs and a living room below, suitable for longer stays or families with older children. All suites include a pillow menu, in-room safe and complimentary Wi-Fi.

"The suite was massive — a full sofa area, a proper work desk, a walk-in wardrobe. Breakfast was varied and freshly made. The pool on the 8th floor was quiet and the golf-course view below it was strangely beautiful. We kept extending our stay."

The location works better than it might appear on first glance. BTS Ratchadamri (Silom Line) is a three-minute walk — one stop connects to BTS Sala Daeng / MRT Silom, while heading in the other direction you reach BTS Chidlom in two minutes and BTS Ploenchit shortly after. CentralWorld is a ten-minute walk or two BTS stops. Central Embassy and Gaysorn Village are within comfortable reach. Lumphini Park is approximately fifteen minutes on foot to the south. The lane itself is quiet — no through-traffic, no bar noise — which means the hotel delivers a degree of residential calm that is unusual for a property so close to Bangkok's main shopping corridor.

The standout facility for most guests is the 8th-floor infinity-edge pool and Jacuzzi. At 94 rooms, Hansar is a small hotel, so the pool rarely crowds — early-morning swimmers in particular describe it as feeling like a private pool, with the fairways and trees of the Royal Sports Club spread out below and Bangkok's skyline rising beyond them. The pool deck also connects to Elefin Café's outdoor terrace, making post-swim breakfast a natural flow. Below the pool level, the 24-hour fitness centre is compact but well equipped. Hansar Thai Wellness provides traditional Thai massage and spa treatments on dedicated floors; Luxsa Clinic operates as a certified medical wellness centre for guests seeking structured health programmes rather than casual spa visits — an unusual differentiator that draws both local and international clients.

The food and beverage programme punches above the hotel's size. Elefin Café serves breakfast (included for all suites until 10 am) with a rotating selection of à la carte hot dishes, fresh tropical fruit, pastries and an egg station — a provision praised in almost every review. Arizuki is the headline dining venue: a Japanese restaurant whose head chef trained in Japan and whose seafood-forward menu is consistently described by reviewers as feeling more like a specialist neighbourhood restaurant than a hotel F&B outlet. Italian Osteria covers evening Italian options, while Rouge Bar serves cocktails throughout the day.

There are honest points to factor in before booking. Reviews across Booking.com and Trip.com mention that some bathrooms show signs of age — slow-draining baths, occasional plumbing inconsistencies, and bathroom linens that do not always meet expectations for a five-star at this price point. Neither issue is universal, but both recur often enough to be worth noting; the front-desk team resolves maintenance requests quickly when guests report them on arrival. A THB 2,000-per-night security deposit is collected at check-in and returned at check-out — standard practice but higher than some guests expect and worth factoring into your cash planning. Breakfast service ends at 10 am, which is shorter than most comparable five-stars; late risers on a leisure trip may find this limiting. Staff quality is described as generally excellent, though a handful of reviews flag occasional inconsistency at the reservations desk.

Suite rates start from approx. THB 3,800–5,500/night for a Luxury Suite outside the high season, rising to THB 5,500–8,000 during the November-to-February peak. The Duplex Suite begins around THB 8,500. Breakfast for two is included at every rate level, which narrows the effective cost gap versus competitors that charge separately for breakfast. Compared with the broader five-star Chidlom–Ploenchit corridor, Hansar sits meaningfully below Park Hyatt Bangkok and Sindhorn Kempinski in headline rate while offering superior suite sizes to most of its neighbours. For travellers whose priorities are space, residential quiet, a genuine golf-course or city view, and breakfast taken care of — all within three minutes of the BTS — this property makes a strong case.

honestSummary: Hansar Bangkok's core offer is the best suite-size-to-price ratio in the Chidlom–Ratchadamri corridor — all-suite accommodation from 59 sqm with breakfast included and an infinity pool overlooking a real golf course, at rates that undercut Park Hyatt and Sindhorn Kempinski by a meaningful margin. The honest caveats are bathroom ageing in some suites and a security deposit higher than guests often anticipate. If generous space, a quiet lane, a green view and breakfast already sorted are your priorities — and BTS Ratchadamri three minutes away handles the rest — Hansar Bangkok is a strong and often underrated choice.
honestChecks: If the golf-course view matters to you — request a Horizon Suite or specify the Royal Sports Club-facing side when booking. Suites on the other side overlook the lane or neighbouring buildings and lack the property's signature green panorama.

If bathroom condition is important — a subset of reviews report plumbing issues in certain suite numbers. Report any problem at the first opportunity on arrival: the front-desk team is rated as responsive and resolves maintenance requests the same day when notified promptly.

If comparing within the Chidlom–Ploenchit five-star bracket — Park Hyatt Bangkok (BTS Ploenchit, two stops away) and Sindhorn Kempinski (Lang Suan) both offer more extensive spa and fitness facilities, though at notably higher rates. Hansar wins clearly on suite size per baht and the breakfast-included angle.

tips.title: Swim before 8 am for a near-private pool
tips.body: The 8th-floor infinity pool is open to all 94 suites, but at that scale the pool rarely feels crowded. The very early morning window — before breakfast service at Elefin Café peaks — gives you the pool almost entirely to yourself, with soft morning light over the Royal Sports Club fairways below. On weekday mornings especially, it can feel like a resort pool rather than a city hotel.

tips.title: Breakfast closes at 10 am — plan accordingly
tips.body: Elefin Café's breakfast service runs only until 10 am, which is shorter than most five-stars at this price. If you tend to sleep late on holiday, it's worth setting an alarm — reviewers consistently rate the breakfast as one of the property's highlights (the à la carte egg station, fresh tropical fruit and daily pastries), and missing it would be a shame.

tips.title: Book Arizuki in advance
tips.body: Arizuki's Japanese dining is widely praised and not just by guests already staying at the hotel — it draws diners from the neighbourhood. The restaurant is compact (as you would expect in a 94-suite boutique), so tables fill up on evenings when multiple groups arrive. Contact the hotel to reserve a table at least a day ahead, especially over weekends or Thai public holidays.

tips.title: Exit BTS Ratchadamri from Exit 2 then follow the lane
tips.body: From BTS Ratchadamri, take Exit 2 and walk along Rajadamri Road for a short stretch before turning into Soi Mahadlekluang 2 — the hotel is at the end of the lane on the left side, approximately three minutes from the station. The entrance signage is understated (by design), so on your first visit have Google Maps open: search 'Hansar Bangkok' for a direct pin.

faq.q: Which BTS station is closest to Hansar Bangkok, and how far is the walk?
faq.a: BTS Ratchadamri (Silom Line) is approximately a three-minute walk from the hotel. Exit at Exit 2, walk along Rajadamri Road and turn into Soi Mahadlekluang 2. One stop towards the city reaches BTS Sala Daeng / MRT Silom; one stop the other direction reaches BTS Chidlom.

faq.q: Does Hansar Bangkok include breakfast? What is the room rate?
faq.a: Breakfast for two is included in every suite at every rate level — no add-on required. Luxury Suite rates start from approx. THB 3,800–5,500/night outside the high season. During the November-to-February peak, expect THB 5,500–8,000 for the same category. Duplex Suite from around THB 8,500. The breakfast inclusion brings the effective cost per person-night down meaningfully compared with hotels that charge for it separately.

faq.q: Is Hansar Bangkok truly all-suite? What is the smallest room size?
faq.a: Yes — every one of Hansar Bangkok's 94 rooms is a suite. The smallest category (Luxury Suite and Horizon Suite) is 59 sqm; the largest (Duplex Suite) is 125 sqm across two floors. All suites have a separate living area, a marble bathroom with both rain shower and soaking bath, and floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows.

faq.q: Is the Royal Sports Club golf-course view worth requesting?
faq.a: Very much so. The Horizon Suite and golf-course-facing suites are among the most praised rooms in recent reviews for the visual contrast they provide — a wide expanse of green fairways directly outside the window, with Bangkok's skyline rising beyond it. It is one of the few genuinely green views available from a five-star hotel in central Bangkok. Specify this preference at booking time, as suites on the opposite side face the lane or neighbouring buildings.

faq.q: What is Luxsa Clinic at Hansar Bangkok?
faq.a: Luxsa Clinic is a certified medical wellness centre operating within the hotel, offering structured health programmes — nutritional guidance, body composition assessments, IV therapies and targeted treatments — rather than standard spa services. It is separate from Hansar Thai Wellness, which focuses on traditional Thai massage and body treatments. Having both under one roof is an unusual offering for a boutique property of this size.
